course.title: Professional Mindset and Leadership Development
course.description: This course develops the professional mindset and leadership competencies necessary for future data science and engineering professionals. With an approach of Scenario-Based Learning (SBL), students will engage in realistic, human-centered activities, such as role-plays, simulations, group discussions, and recorded presentations. These activities are helpful to them in exploring key themes in the course which also includes personal development, resilience, teamwork, communication, ethics, and adaptive leadership. The course emphasizes self-leadership, interpersonal communication, and professional growth, enabling students to apply leadership principles and reflective practice to real-world professional contexts. A series of assessment in this course also includes a recorded PowerPoint presentation for the Leadership Roadmap Project which showcases students’ understanding, self-reflection, and readiness for leadership in the engineering field. The course progresses from self-awareness and personal mindset development to communication, teamwork, and leadership application, concluding with an integrative career and leadership roadmap. This progression reflects the leadership growth stages of self, others, and system.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Professional Mindset and Leadership
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the concept of professional mindset and leadership in engineering contexts. LLO2: Identify key characteristics of professional behaviour and responsibility.

topics.title: Topic 2: Self-awareness, Values, and Resilience
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the role of self-awareness and personal values in professional development. LLO2: Apply strategies for building resilience in academic and professional settings.

topics.title: Topic 3: Empathy and Ethical Practice
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the importance of empathy and ethical decision-making in teamwork. LLO2: Demonstrate ethical reasoning in professional scenarios.

topics.title: Topic 4: Written Communication
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Produce clear and structured professional written communication. LLO2: Apply appropriate tone and organisation in technical writing.

topics.title: Topic 5: Technical Writing & Resume
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Produce clear and structured professional written communication. LLO2: Apply appropriate tone and organisation in technical writing.

topics.title: Topic 6: Interpersonal Communication

topics.title: Topic 7: Digital Communication
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply professional etiquette in digital communication. LLO2: Develop clear and effective multimedia presentations.

topics.title: Topic 8: Teamwork and Situational Leadership

topics.title: Topic 9: Midterm Exam and Review

topics.title: Topic 11: Decision Bias and Cognitive Leadership

topics.title: Topic 12: Cross-Cultural Communication and Cultural Intelligence (CQ)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain cultural differences in communication and leadership. LLO2: Apply cultural intelligence in diverse team interactions.

topics.title: Topic 13: Work-Life Balance & Well-Being
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the relationship between well-being and professional performance. LLO2: Apply strategies for maintaining work-life balance.

topics.title: Topic 14: Leading Change and Adaptability
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain challenges in organisational change. LLO2: Apply leadership strategies to support adaptation and innovation.

topics.title: Topic 15: Final Showcase: Leadership and Career Roadmap
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Integrate leadership concepts into a personal development plan. LLO2: Present a structured leadership and career roadmap.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Students are expected to: - Complete assigned readings before each class and prepare for discussion. - Actively participate in role plays, simulations, and peer feedback. - Submit all assignments and final projects on time through a digital platform given. - Maintain a minimum of 80 % attendance to qualify for assessment. - Exhibit professional conduct and ethical behaviour in all course activities. - Use feedback constructively to improve leadership and communication skills. - Demonstrate integrity, no plagiarism, AI misuse, or unauthorized collaboration.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Minimum 80 % attendance required. Readings must be completed before and/or after class; active participation is mandatory. Academic Integrity Plagiarism, AI-generated content without acknowledgment, and cheating are strictly prohibited. All assignments must be original and submitted individually unless group work is specified. Assignments and Deadlines Late submission penalty: 10 % per day unless excused in advance. Extensions are granted only for documented reasons. Professional Conduct Respect and collaboration are expected in all activities. Mobile devices used only for learning or recording purposes. Final Project Students must submit a recorded Power-Point presentation (10 - 15 minutes) and one-page reflection note by Week 16. Students will receive in-class guidance during Weeks 14 - 15 and may consult online with the instructor before the submission deadline.
